subject: health
unitTitle: Safety, Injury Prevention, and Digital Life
title: Guided practice: medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety
focus: medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety
essentialQuestion: How do I prevent harm and respond well when something goes wrong?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Medicine is given by a trusted adult only, at the right dose, and is never shared.
Prescription medicine belongs to one named person; taking someone else's is dangerous.
Alcohol, nicotine, vapes, and other drugs affect a developing brain more than an adult one.
Vapes are not harmless water vapour; most contain nicotine, which is addictive.
Never taste or sniff an unlabelled substance.
If someone has swallowed something, tell an adult at once — speed matters.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I explain medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.

explanation.heading: Understand medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety
paragraphs: Medicine is given by a trusted adult only, at the right dose, and is never shared.
Prescription medicine belongs to one named person; taking someone else's is dangerous.
Alcohol, nicotine, vapes, and other drugs affect a developing brain more than an adult one.

explanation.importantDistinction: Learning about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety supports accurate reasoning and safe next steps; it does not authorize a diagnosis, individualized treatment advice, a person label, or a value judgment.
explanation.decisionRule: SITUATION: Name the facts. CHOICES: Compare safe options. INFORMATION: Use what matters. HELP: Name the responsible adult or source.

canonicalPracticeContext.heading: Use the authored practice situation
canonicalPracticeContext.situation: An older student says vaping is "just flavoured air" and offers one. Give two accurate facts in reply and say what you do next.
canonicalPracticeContext.treatment: This canonical context may support teaching or discussion. It does not replace the separate fresh independent, mastery, or remediation-retry cases.

modelExample.heading: Watch the reasoning: medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety
modelExample.situation: A fictional Northside group must choose a next step about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. The stated situation includes this fact: Medicine is given by a trusted adult only, at the right dose, and is never shared. The group may pause and gather relevant information, ask the responsible adult or professional, or act immediately from an unsupported guess.
relevantFacts: Medicine is given by a trusted adult only, at the right dose, and is never shared.
Prescription medicine belongs to one named person; taking someone else's is dangerous.
modelExample.assumptionOrDistraction: A popular or confident statement about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety is not automatically accurate and cannot establish a person's health, motives, or character.
possibleActions: Use the stated fact, compare safe options, and ask the responsible help source.
Act alone from the unsupported guess.
Ask a fictional person to reveal private information before helping.
modelExample.successCheck: The model uses the lesson fact, explains the connection, stays within the learner role, and names responsible help when it is needed.
workedReasoning: List only the stated situation and constraints before judging an option.
Compare at least two safe choices using the lesson facts and reject choices that depend on guessing or acting beyond the learner role.
Choose a feasible next step and identify the adult, professional, service, or authority responsible for help.

guidedReasoning.heading: Try a different case with support
guidedReasoning.situation: A fictional Riverside youth group must explain or act on medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. The group has this reliable lesson information: Prescription medicine belongs to one named person; taking someone else's is dangerous. It has not been given any person's private health information.
availableChoices: Use the stated facts and compare safe options.
Pause and contact the responsible help source.
turnOne: Name an adult who can help.
guidedReasoning.cue: Look for the situation, safe choices, relevant information, and who can help.
feedbackMoves: If a response adds a guess, replace it with a fact from the case or lesson.
If medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety is named without explanation, link one fact to the concept or process.
If a choice is reasonable but the reason is missing, add the fact that supports it.
If a response seeks disclosure, diagnoses, shames, or exceeds the learner role, switch to the fictional facts and the approved help route.
Accept an equivalent typed, handwritten, drawn-and-labeled, signed, selected, or spoken response when it shows the same reasoning.
guidedReasoning.turnTwo: Fix one sentence. Use a fact and a safe next step.
guidedReasoning.releaseCondition: Continue when the response uses a stated fact, applies medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety, and gives a safe next step without private disclosure or a person label.

typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking

freshMasteryCheck.heading: Check the idea in a new place
freshMasteryCheck.situation: A fictional Lakeside school committee reviews medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. The committee knows: Alcohol, nicotine, vapes, and other drugs affect a developing brain more than an adult one. It must correct one unsupported claim and choose a safe next step.
freshMasteryCheck.freshnessNote: This case is different from the model, guided case, and independent case. Do not copy their conclusions.

remediation.heading: Try a different model
remediation.trigger: Use this route after an observable gap in a fact, vocabulary meaning, reasoning step, process order, or help route for medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety.
remediation.prerequisite: First restate this approved fact in your own words: Medicine is given by a trusted adult only, at the right dose, and is never shared.
remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a four-box decision map: SITUATION, SAFE CHOICES, RELEVANT INFORMATION, and HELP. Fill each box with case facts before writing a conclusion.
contrast: Sufficient: uses a stated fact about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety, explains the connection, and stays within the learner role.
Needs revision: repeats a topic word, adds a guess, or gives an action with no factual reason or responsible help source.
remediation.guidedCorrection: Cross out the guess. Circle the fact. Add one safe action.

freshRetry.situation: A fictional Oak Street library receives a new question about medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety. Staff provide this approved fact: Prescription medicine belongs to one named person; taking someone else's is dangerous. The learner must respond without using the Northside, Riverside, Maple, or Lakeside conclusions.

remediation.exitCriterion: Return to the independent route when the learner accurately uses a fact, applies medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety, explains a safe response, and identifies support without answer-bearing help.
remediation.nextRoute: If the same gap remains, return to the named prerequisite with an adult instructor; do not replace the task with private reflection.

laterTransfer.timing: Use in a later lesson or a separate session.
laterTransfer.prompt: Apply medicines, household chemicals, and substance safety to a meaningfully different fictional or public case. Retrieve the concept, use relevant facts, justify a safe response, and identify the responsible support or authority route.
laterTransfer.masteryBoundary: The current independent response is one evidence occasion. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence now and accurate later retrieval or transfer.
